data.name: Report_LgProfile_Body
data.value: This section summarizes the basic context used for the ROSRA assessment, including the local government, financial year, currency, current own-source revenue, gross regional product and population. These inputs define the scope of the analysis and ensure that the results refer to the same jurisdiction and reporting year.

data.name: Report_QuickEstimate_Body
data.value: This section provides a high-level estimate of the overall room for own-source revenue improvement. It is intended to give users an initial sense of the scale of the opportunity before moving into the stream-level diagnosis. The estimate should be read as an orientation point, not as a detailed explanation of where revenue is being lost.

data.name: Report_StreamGap_What
data.value: This section shows the estimated functional gap for each revenue stream included in the assessment. The visual breaks each stream into the main types of revenue loss: compliance, coverage, and liability or valuation. The bars allow users to compare the relative size of gaps across streams, while the colored segments show what is driving the gap within each stream.

data.name: Report_StreamGap_Why
data.value: This helps users move beyond a general statement that revenue collection is low and identify whether the problem is mainly linked to unpaid bills, missing taxpayers or units, weak assessment, or a combination of issues.

data.name: Report_StreamGap_How
data.value: Read the chart from the largest to the smallest stream gap. Use the table below the chart to check the estimated amount by gap type and the total estimated gap for each stream.

data.name: Report_StreamPrio_What
data.value: Stream prioritization ranks the revenue streams included in the assessment according to their total functional gap. This helps users see which streams represent the largest estimated opportunity for improvement within the current diagnosis.

data.name: Report_StreamPrio_Why
data.value: Local governments often have several revenue streams but limited time, staff and reform capacity. Prioritization helps focus attention on the streams where improvement could make the biggest difference, while still allowing users to adjust the sequence based on local context.

data.name: Report_StreamPrio_How
data.value: The table is ordered from the largest to the smallest estimated stream gap. Streams marked as excluded are not included in the share calculation or downstream recommendations because they do not apply to the local government or were removed from the assessment.

data.name: Report_GapPrio_What
data.value: Gap prioritization breaks each prioritized stream into the specific types of problems driving underperformance. It shows whether the issue is related to compliance, coverage, valuation, liability assessment, or mixed gaps.

data.name: Report_GapPrio_Why
data.value: Different gaps require different types of reform. A compliance gap may require better billing, reminders, payment channels or enforcement. A coverage gap may require better registration, data matching or field verification. A valuation or liability gap may require better assessment rules, updated values or clearer fee-setting.

data.name: Report_GapPrio_How
data.value: For each stream, the table shows the selected prioritization mode and the suggested order of gap types. The order should be read as a starting point for reform sequencing and can be adjusted based on feasibility, capacity, political considerations or ongoing reforms.

data.name: Report_ReformGuidance_Body
data.value: Based on the prioritized streams and gap types, ROSRA identifies relevant reform options in the Recommendations section of the platform. This report does not reproduce the full solution catalogue. Users should refer to the website to review the selected solution cards, including implementation steps, timeline, feasibility considerations, stakeholders and monitoring guidance.
